subject.title: fix(agents): bound IDENTITY.md reads to prevent OOM

question: Should workspace identity loading and explicit --identity-file imports both reject files larger than the shared 2 MiB workspace bootstrap limit?
rationale: The cap prevents unbounded allocation but intentionally makes previously accepted large identity files fail, so tests cannot determine the repository’s desired compatibility boundary.

options.title: Accept the shared 2 MiB cap
options.body: Use the existing workspace bootstrap limit for both paths, then merge after the requested exact-head CLI proof is supplied.

options.title: Choose an identity-specific cap
options.body: Select and document a different identity-file limit while retaining the same bounded reader and regression coverage.

options.title: Preserve uncapped imports
options.body: Keep one or both paths compatible with arbitrarily large files, accepting the existing memory-exhaustion exposure.

recommendation.title: Accept the shared 2 MiB cap
recommendation.body: Use the existing workspace bootstrap limit for both paths, then merge after the requested exact-head CLI proof is supplied.

likelyOwner.reason: The identity parsing and config flow appears to originate from their merged feature work, making them the strongest available owner for its input compatibility contract.
